title: Uniquely 3-edge-colourable cubic graphs are Hamiltonian
statement: Let $G$ be a finite simple graph that is $3$-regular and admits a proper $3$-edge-colouring. If $G$ is uniquely $3$-edge-colourable — meaning any two proper $3$-edge-colourings of $G$ agree up to a permutation of the three colours — then $G$ contains a Hamiltonian cycle, that is, a closed walk that visits every vertex exactly once.
hypotheses_covered: G is a finite simple graph
